solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Without afterthought, cops now stick together (6)

indicatorNotes.Without afterthought: an afterthought in a letter is a PS, so 'without' it means those two letters go

blocks.note: here = now, as in 'here and now'

annotation.surface: A police squad, resolving not to second-guess, closes ranks.
annotation.walkthrough: An afterthought is a PS, the postscript tacked onto a letter; take it off COPS and only CO remains.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things that cohere hold together, literally like particles or figuratively like an argument.

entries.clue: Cleaner wrongly supporting Greek cook (9)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits below it

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
GR is the abbreviation for Greek

annotation.surface: A domestic cleaner is wrongly backing a Greek chef in some kitchen dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' looks like an anagram signal, but it is simply ILL, placed under GR because it is 'supporting' in a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: To chargrill is to cook over high heat so the surface chars.

entries.clue: This naked boy turned up and shot Spanish gent (7)

indicatorNotes.naked: stripped of its outer letters, THIS loses T and S
indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turned up means written bottom to top

blocks.note: a shot = a go, a turn at something

annotation.surface: A naked boy appears and shoots a Spanish gentleman: a lurid news story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' is a noun here, a go at something, not a gunshot. A hidalgo is a member of the lower Spanish nobility.
annotation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish gentleman of the minor nobility.

entries.clue: Retired old man’s boring meal (6)

indicatorNotes.boring: one thing boring into another sits inside it

blocks.note: RET is the abbreviation for retired

annotation.surface: A pensioner's father makes a tedious lunch companion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' pretends to describe the dull meal or old man, but it is a placement instruction; RET is the standard abbreviation for retired.
annotation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, a formal or literary word for one.

entries.clue: Taps into data and nicks stuff (7)

indicatorNotes.into: the taps go into the data word

blocks.note: taps are marked C and H, cold and hot

annotation.surface: A hacker taps into data and steals things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taps' is not phone-tapping but the two taps over a sink, labelled C and H, which go inside FILES.
annotation.definitionFit: To filch is to steal, so filches means nicks stuff; nick is British slang for steal.

entries.clue: Ludicrous situation in remote church (5)

annotation.surface: Something absurd is going on in an isolated church.
annotation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the usual crossword shorthand for church.
annotation.definitionFit: Farce is first a stage comedy of wild improbability, and by extension any real situation that absurd.

entries.clue: Most wary of learner driver on scary road (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, a piece on another comes above it

annotation.surface: A nervous learner is most cautious of a frightening road.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, so 'learner driver' gives just L.
annotation.definitionFit: Leery means wary or suspicious, so leeriest is most wary.

entries.clue: Contemptuous expression upset one Tuesday regular (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset means turned over, read bottom to top

blocks.note: TUE is the abbreviation for Tuesday

annotation.surface: Someone sneers, annoyed by a person who turns up every Tuesday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal, but in a down entry it turns BAH over.
annotation.definitionFit: A habitué is a regular visitor to a place.

entries.clue: Sharp turn (5)

blocks.note: sharp in the sense of steep, as a cliff face
turn as a verb: swerve, change course, as a ship does

annotation.surface: A sharp turn on a road.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one phrase, a sharp turn, but it splits into two meanings: sheer as steep and sheer as swerve.
annotation.definitionFit: Sheer means very steep, and to sheer (off) is to change course abruptly.

entries.clue: Constant excitement and drinking (8)

blocks.note: c is the constant for the speed of light

annotation.surface: A description of a party that is all thrills and booze.
annotation.walkthrough: C is the scientific constant for the speed of light, a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A carousal is a drinking bout, a spell of noisy drinking.

entries.clue: Fit dad cycling along (3,2)

indicatorNotes.cycling: cycling moves the last letter round to the front

blocks.note: DAD with its last D moved to the front
up = along, as in 'walk up the road'

annotation.surface: A healthy father pedals along on his bike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like it describes the dad, but it is the definition, a verb: a story that fits adds up.
annotation.definitionFit: When facts fit together they add up, make sense.

entries.clue: Appealing E in Algebra, unfortunately, and English (9)

indicatorNotes.in: E goes in with the letters of ALGEBRA
indicatorNotes.unfortunately: things that turn out unfortunately go wrong, so the letters end up in the wrong order
indicatorNotes.and: 'and' simply adds the next piece, so English is tacked on after the jumbled letters

annotation.surface: A school report bemoans a lowly E grade in algebra and in English too.
annotation.walkthrough: An E is a poor exam grade, so the surface reads as a bad report card, far from anything appealing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something agreeable pleases you, which is what appealing means.

entries.clue: Calculus vexes tenor (9)

annotation.surface: A singer is annoyed by his maths homework.
annotation.walkthrough: Calculus is not the maths but its medical sense, a stone formed in the body; tenor is the tone of something, not a singer.
annotation.definitionFit: A calculus is a stone formed in an organ, and a gallstone is one in the gall bladder.

entries.clue: At home with half-sister in Bury (5)

indicatorNotes.half-: read as an instruction, 'half' asks for half of the word it is attached to, here the last three letters of SISTER

annotation.surface: Someone lives at home with a half-sister in Bury, a town near Manchester.
annotation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, and the capital letter hides that it is the verb. Half-sister looks like a relation but gives half of SISTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to inter is to place a body in the earth, from Latin terra.

entries.clue: Press club (4)

blocks.note: press as in smoothing creases out of clothes
club as in golf: a metal-headed one

annotation.surface: A club for journalists.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press club' reads as a journalists' club, but it is two separate words: the laundry verb and the golf club.
annotation.definitionFit: Iron means to press clothes, and an iron is a kind of golf club.

entries.clue: Fools small people with essentially untrustworthy evaluation (10)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its central letter

annotation.surface: Short folk are misjudged as fools by an untrustworthy appraisal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' asks for the essence of UNTRUSTWORTHY, its single central letter, not a synonym for untrustworthy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to assess something is to evaluate it, and the noun follows.

entries.clue: Nonchalance in a sense is affected (8)

indicatorNotes.affected: the letters are altered, worked on

annotation.surface: A remark that casual indifference is, in a way, just a pose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Affected' reads as 'put on', which suits nonchalance, but it tells you to rearrange A SENSE IS.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: nonchalance is being at ease, unbothered, and this answer names that state.

entries.clue: Elite go to bed drunk, according to Spooner (3-6)

indicatorNotes.according to Spooner: swap the opening sounds of two words, as Rev. Spooner did

blocks.note: to flop is to collapse into bed
the two opening sounds, FL and T, change places

annotation.surface: Members of the elite stagger off to bed drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: Swapping the initial sounds of FLOP and TIGHT gives TOP and FLIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest class, elite.

entries.clue: Protestant clumsily dropping books in part of church (8)

indicatorNotes.dropping: the named letters are left out

blocks.note: OT, the Old Testament books, is left out of PROTESTANT

annotation.surface: A Protestant drops a pile of hymnbooks while crossing the church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' is OT, the Old Testament; remove it from PROTESTANT and rearrange what is left.
annotation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, crossing the nave.

entries.clue: Plebeian girl following cow about (5-5)

indicatorNotes.following: the girl comes after the other pieces

blocks.note: a cow lows, so it is a lower

annotation.surface: A common girl trails around after a cow on a farm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cow' suggests intimidate, but here it is the animal that lows, giving LOWER; C is circa, about.
annotation.definitionFit: Plebeians were the common people of ancient Rome, so the adjective means of the common people.

entries.clue: Wife heartlessly walloping fish (7)

indicatorNotes.heartlessly: the heart, or middle letter, is taken out

blocks.note: HITTING with its central T removed

annotation.surface: A cruel wife is beating someone with a fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' seems to describe the wife's cruelty; it removes the middle T of HITTING.
annotation.definitionFit: A whiting is a sea fish of the cod family.

entries.clue: Look back, and carry on (4)

indicatorNotes.back: a word going back runs from its end to its start, so it is written in reverse

annotation.surface: Glance behind you and then continue on your way.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Look back' read as glancing behind you; it is the reversal of a four-letter word for look.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to keep on, or keep going, is to continue, so the verb alone can mean carry on.

entries.clue: Gourmet in despair, oddly lacking salt? (7)

indicatorNotes.oddly lacking: the odd-numbered letters are the ones missing

blocks.note: salting is one way to cure meat; the question mark flags the example

annotation.surface: A food lover is in despair because his dish has no salt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly lacking' reads as 'strangely missing' in the surface, but it strips the odd letters from DESPAIR.
annotation.definitionFit: An epicure is a gourmet, a person devoted to fine food.

entries.clue: Tricky question of China losing grip (6)

blocks.note: TEA SERVICE without VICE, a gripping tool

annotation.surface: A puzzle about China loosening its grip on a region.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C makes China look like the country; it is crockery, a TEA SERVICE, which loses VICE, the clamp that grips.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a teaser teases the mind, so it is a puzzle or tricky question.

entries.clue: Stones murderer, stifling resistance (5)

indicatorNotes.stifling: the murderer smothers R, holding it inside

blocks.note: Cain, the first murderer in the Bible
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

annotation.surface: A murderer smothers a victim who resists, then hurls stones.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stones' is the definition, not the Rolling Stones or a weapon: a cairn is a heap of stones.
annotation.definitionFit: A cairn is a mound of stones set up as a marker or memorial.

entries.clue: Mafia boss ultimately shown to be chicken (5)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: capo = head of a Mafia family

annotation.surface: A feared Mafia boss is finally exposed as a coward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' reads as coward, but it is the bird: a capon is a castrated cockerel.
annotation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for eating, so a chicken.

entries.clue: Friendly clot clutching nickel (9)

indicatorNotes.clutching: the outer word holds the other inside

blocks.note: Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

annotation.surface: A friendly idiot is gripping a coin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clot' is British slang for a fool, which the surface uses, but here it is the verb, congeal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: congenial company is pleasant and friendly to be with.

entries.clue: Tough hack entering empty city (5)

indicatorNotes.entering: something entering a place goes inside it, so the hack word sits within the other
indicatorNotes.empty: CITY with its inside taken out leaves C…Y

annotation.surface: A hard-bitten journalist walks into a deserted city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist, but it is the verb hew, to chop.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym for food: tough meat or toffee needs a lot of chewing, and that is what the answer describes.

entries.clue: Pericles dancing with son is very amusing (9)

indicatorNotes.dancing: a dancer moves about and changes position, as the letters must
indicatorNotes.with: 'with' brings the son in alongside the name, adding S to the letters

annotation.surface: The Athenian statesman Pericles dancing with his son is a hilarious sight.
annotation.walkthrough: Priceless in the informal sense of hilarious, not of great value.
annotation.definitionFit: Priceless informally means extremely funny.

entries.clue: Golf fanatics retiring hurt (5)

blocks.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Golf obsessives leave the course injured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests golfers quitting hurt; it reverses the letters. G comes from the phonetic alphabet (Alpha, Bravo… Golf).
annotation.definitionFit: Stung means hurt, physically or in feelings.

entries.clue: Bold on the phone at the end of each day (7)

annotation.definition: at the end of each day

indicatorNotes.on the phone: heard over the phone, so it goes by sound

annotation.surface: Someone is brazen on the telephone every evening.
annotation.walkthrough: The K of KNIGHTLY is silent, so it sounds just like NIGHTLY.
annotation.definitionFit: Nightly means happening every night, at the end of each day.

entries.clue: Some masseur gently pressing (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the letters, a run from inside the phrase

annotation.surface: A masseur is pressing gently on a client's back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' belongs to the massage picture, but it is the definition, meaning urgent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pressing matter pushes for attention now, which is what urgent means.
